parameters.content:
## Discord channel alerts by email

### How it works
This workflow is for members of Discord servers who must not miss a message, for example the trade calls of a signal channel. Every 15 minutes, it reads the channels you list, one after another, in your own Chrome. It keeps only the messages that came since the last check, and sends you one email from your Gmail with them: author, time, text, attachment and embed links, and a link to each message. A check with no new message sends nothing.

The first run sends no email. It only records the last message of each channel. The emails start with the next new messages.

Each run opens Discord and Gmail in your Chrome. Discord lets one tab of an account at a time: a check fails when Discord is open in another tab, and the next one reads the messages it missed.

### Setup
- Install the community node `@reduck-ai/n8n-nodes-reduck` (self-hosted n8n only): https://docs.reduck.ai/n8n/#quick-start
- Make a Reduck account, and select an API key from https://reduck.ai/api-keys in one Reduck node.
- Install the Reduck extension in Chrome, sign in to Discord and Gmail there, and keep Chrome open.
- In **Config**, set:
  - `channels`: one channel per line, as `Label | channel URL`, e.g. `Calls | https://discord.com/channels/123/456`. Copy the URL from the channel in Discord on the web.
  - `email_to`: where the alerts go, e.g. `you@example.com`.
  - `gmail_account`: the Gmail address that sends them, when Chrome has several.
- Publish the workflow.

### Customization
Change the schedule, or raise `messages_per_read` for a busy channel.

## Read the setup
The channels to read, and the last message already sent for each one.

## Read each channel
One channel at a time: Discord lets one tab of an account at a time.

## Email the new messages
Only the messages after the last one recorded. No new message: no email.

## Record the last message
After the email, so a failed email is sent again by the next run.
